newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE OPPOSITION ALLIANCE BACKS MERCOSUR BLOC.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE OPPOSITION ALLIANCE BACKS MERCOSUR BLOC.

text.p: Argentina's new opposition alliance made a strong commitment Wednesday to Mercosur, the fledgling South American trade bloc that groups Argentina with Brazil and Paraguay and Uruguay.

The Radical Party/Frepaso alliance has been eager to reassure the public it will not upset the economy if it gains power. Its formation earlier this month has raised the first real threat to the Peronist majority in Congress and to the governing party's hold on the presidency after Carlos Menem steps down in 1999.
As part of the confidence-building efforts, Frepaso coaltion leader Carlos Alvarez and Radical Party chief Rodolfo Terragno paid a visit to Brazilian Ambassador Luis Felipe de Seixas.
Alvarez later told reporters that the Mercosur customs union, launched in 1995, "has been one policy where there has been no argument" with the Peronists.
The Frepaso leader said the alliance's policy proposals would be to "reinforce and continue Mercosur policy" but with "some differences."
"We must make the Mercosur more institutional, so that there are no more surprises, to provide clear rules of the game so that one country cannot impose its policies on another," he said.
In its short life, Mercosur has already been shaken by Brazil's imposing import limitations without warning or consulting its new trade partners.
But it has also succeeded in attracting Chile as an associate partner and overtures from Mexico and Canada.

"We would like to underline the strategic importance that we give to the Mercosur, not only as a free-trade agreement but also as a fundamental part of a strategy of socioeconomic development and of international integration," Terragno said.

Early on, the alliance pledged to continue the current policy of pegging the peso at par with the dollar. Known as Convertibility, the currency link is credited with virtually eliminating inflation in Argentina since it was implemented in 1991.
The alliance has also promised not to interfere with privatizations carried out by Menem since he came to power in 1989.
